name: Akum
catalog_citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Übersee 93: 299–326. Hamburg University Press. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215
catalog_locator: §2.3 Tone, p. 306 (minimal pairs pp. 306–307); §7 Verbal morphology, p. 316; §9 Conclusion, p. 324
catalog_quote: 2.3 Tone. Akum has a three-tone system. At this stage of research, we only find lexically distinctive tones in Akum. However, as data from other Jukunoid languages suggests (Storch 1999; Kempf 2017), tone may also play a significant role at the grammatical level. 2.3.1 Minimal pairs. The following minimal pairs show the role of tone in distinguishing lexical items. ... L vs. M kàm [110Hz (m)] ‘tell’ ... kām [155 (m)] ‘meet’ ... Tonal triplets cɔ̀ [165Hz (f)] ‘sing’ cɔ̄ [190Hz (f)] ‘fall’ cʊ́ [200Hz (f)] ‘descend’ ... [§7, p. 316:] The verbal root in Akum has the syllable structure CV or CVC. ... The root vowel bears one of the three lexical tones: L, M or H.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The 'tonal' coding rests on the only grammar-class description of Akum that exists (Kempf & Prischnegg 2020, peer-reviewed, open access, by the fieldworkers, with Hz-measured tonal minimal pairs and triplets), which we hold as publisher PDF + text; the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated pages (306-307, 316). The sketch positively establishes a three-level lexical tone system (L/M/H plus falling/rising contours) and nowhere mentions stress or accent, so 'tonal, domain unstated' is the faithful reading. Caveat worth keeping in mind but not actionable: the authors label their phonology 'tentative' given ~20 h of data, so absence of a stress statement is silence rather than a denial. No better source exists to download; the two unheld items (Prischnegg's 2008 comparative Yukuben dissertation, print-only; the 2002/2005 SIL survey wordlist) are low-yield for prosody. downloaded bibliograph

sources.note: Contains Prischnegg's 2004-07 Nigerian Akum (Shibong) field data that the 2020 sketch draws on; Glottolog codes ~30 pp as bearing on Akum [aku]. Only other primary linguistic treatment; could state explicitly whether any accent/prominence was observed alongside the three tones. Comparative in focus, so payoff is modest.
